replicates.rationale: Both explain registration, proxy lookup, inject as dependency, and Fiber lifecycle ownership. A over-specifies unload/hot-reload behavior not supplied by the source, while B keeps the boundary cleaner and simpler.

Both cover all required facts and avoid saying the string is converted into an object. Both infer dependent stop/restart behavior beyond the source, but A states a stronger automatic unload/restart guarantee and adds more unsupported mechanics, so B is better overall.

Both answer the main confusion and support transfer with the provider/consumer distinction. A stays within the source by saying Fiber records/checks dependencies and coordinates lifecycle, while B guarantees consumer cleanup/pause on provider unload and also suggests ctx.llm may still work without inject, which weakens the boundary.

item_observation: The strongest answers distinguish three roles: Service registers the instance by name, Context Proxy resolves ctx.llm from services, and inject declares a required dependency managed by the plugin Fiber without itself constructing or converting anything.
